I have posted this in both /v/ps4 and /v/xboxone as I run both subverses. It is an important time to speak to everyone about this as we are in the beginning stages of this subverse, and we have just hit 1000 subscribers.

First off, let me start off about myself:

I'm mblim, and I used the same username on reddit and it will be my PSN ID as soon as they allow me to change it. I've been on reddit for nearly 5 years (under two different accounts) and digg before then. I am a huge fan of video games. I've been collecting for years for all of the big 3 (Nintendo, Microsoft, and Sony) and I play a ton of video games, which I believe is an important factor in helping see this place thrive. I still have all my Sony consoles, as well as the majority of my old games.

Over the next few days, I'll be changing the subverse style to what I've been working on in /v/leafs. This will give us more options (such as flair, announcements, and a smaller banner so we have more real estate for posts) and a cleaner look. This leads me into what I want to get some feedback from you all.

Transparency: Starting today, I have linked the mod logs into the sidebar, so that you will ALWAYS be able to see what is deleted, why it was deleted, and when it was deleted. You can also see if any users are even banned from the subverse. These are open to discussion, and you will be able to message the moderators. I will ALWAYS leave a comment if I remove a post or a comment. I want the subverse to moderate itself, so please use downvoats to deal with content that is not related to discussion or the PS4 (please do not downvoat if you disagree with an opinion). If you really feel that content needs to be deleted, please message me directly. To show you that the transparency really works, I deleted a post on here a couple of weeks ago. The ability to leave a reason why something has been deleted has not been implemented yet, so when I delete a post I will leave a comment in the thread before doing so. They show up in the mod log.

To answer a question I've been getting a lot, I'm still evaluating how we add moderators to this subverse. I want to make sure I bring in the right people to assist, as I have been getting a lot of requests to be a moderator, especially from people who don't even have day old accounts or have commented/submitted anywhere. I don't want to make any quick decisions as I feel there are some things that can be done better than our reddit counterpart, and I'd love to see this place thrive.

Now my question to you is, what do you think? I want feedback and comments from you guys, and I really want to make this the best place for PS4 discussion. Please give any feedback on the current rules, the subverse style, anything I've said in this post, or anything you'd like to see implemented. You all are the content providers, the discussion builders, the heart and soul of these aggregator sites. You are the core start up users, and I would love your feedback.

Thank you all for reading and your time

-mblim

EDIT: The new theme is somewhat implemented. Much easier on the eyes. Also, there is a dark theme enabled now, so click on the lightbulb by your username in the top right corner to see the dark theme

I wanted to have a discussion regarding the rules that are set in place. Specifically #6. I get "hacking" as in subverting protection measures to gain illegal access to other consoles. Fraud, piracy, account trading... makes sense. Modding. To me, there's a broad range of the term "modding." Such as modding the console case to a cool/fun design. In this case I think that case modding/mods posts should be allowed in this subverse. It's an art that should be encouraged for those interested.

Then there's "hardware/software modding" is a different beast for subverses. Such as mod chips or software hacks. It has the potential for much grey area, such as pirating games or a customized user interface (much like the original xbox when modded). Regardless of the positive over the negatives for hardware modding, it's too much grey area to pick and choose what to allow in a subverse. So, not allowed.

My overall point, to disallow "modding" posts is a bit broad. I would like to see case modding posts in gaming subverses, I'm sure others would as well.

 

tl/dr- Great work! Change "modding" to "hardware/software modding"
